quests.explanation: 'D'you' is a casual spelling of the fast-speech version of 'do you' — that's the phrase it actually represents in natural speech.
quests.hint: Think about what phrase, said quickly and casually, would naturally come out sounding like this.
quests.nativeTip: Focus on vocal flow: do not stop your breath between words. Match the speaker's melodic pitch rather than stressing every word equally.

quests.instruction: Master speech rhythm and shadowing cadence
quests.word: Before the concert ends, I woulda liked to say goodbye.
quests.textToSpeak: Before the concert ends, I woulda liked to say goodbye.
quests.ipa: /bɪˈfɔː ðə ˈkɒnsət endz aɪ ˈwʊdə laɪkt tə seɪ ˌgʊdˈbaɪ/
quests.flowRule: Mastery Integration: real fluent speech combines thought-group pausing with casual reductions and linking all at once — shadowing well means tracking all of these together.
quests.ruleDescription: real fluent speech combines thought-group pausing with casual reductions and linking all at once — shadowing well means tracking all of these together.
quests.explanation: The pause genuinely falls right after 'ends', at the end of the opening phrase, not after 'I' mid-clause; and 'woulda' means 'would have' exactly as described.
quests.hint: Read the whole sentence naturally first, then check that the described pause point matches where you actually paused.
quests.nativeTip: Focus on vocal flow: do not stop your breath between words. Match the speaker's melodic pitch rather than stressing every word equally.
